sentences.text:
Govind Singh Purohith, Son Of Sri Parwar ... vs The State Of
Andhra Pradesh, Rep. By Its on 29 November, 2018
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice P.Keshava Rao
 Writ Petition No.19181 Of 2015
Order:
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 1 to 3.

The prayer sought for in the writ petition is as under:
"to issue a Writ of certiorari or any other appropriate Writ Order or an appropriate direction declaring the Order Dt. 20-05-2015 bearing No. FSS Act C.C. No.
3/FSO/002B/VZM/2015, Passed by the Respondent No. 2 levying the maximum penalty of Rs. 5,00,000-00, as illegal, arbitrary, unreasonable, without jurisdiction,
besides being opposed to the principles of natural justice and set aside the same."
The basic point canvassed by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner is that in the light of the two conflicting reports issued by the Food Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Nacharam,
Hyderabad and the Director, Referral Food Laboratory, Kolkatha, the imposition of penalty of Rs.5.00 lakhs, is arbitrary and illegal.
The respondent No.3 filed a counter affidavit denying the material allegations made in the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition and contended inter alia that the impugned order in the present writ petition is appealable under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

It is also mentioned in the counter affidavit that the State of Andhra Pradesh vide G.O.Rt.No.735, Home (Courts-A) Department, dated 01.07.2015, designated the Principal District & Sessions Judge's Courts in all 13 districts in the State of Andhra Pradesh and the Metropolitan Sessions Judges in the Metropolitan Cities, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam as Food Safety Appellate Tribunals, for trial and disposal of the cases filed under the said Act.
When a statutory alternative appellate remedy is available to the petitioner, this Court is not inclined to entertain the present writ petition.

Further from the perusal of the affidavit, the petitioner has not made out any case seeking indulgence of this Court carving out the three exceptions so as to maintain the present writ petition before this Court.
Even on this aspect also, this Court is not inclined to entertain the writ petition.
Therefore, there are no merits and the writ petition is accordingly dismissed.

At this stage, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner brought to the notice of this Court that at the time of filing of the writ petition, since the Appellate Tribunal was not constituted, the Govind Singh Purohith, Son Of Sri Parwar ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, Rep. By Its on 29 November, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29694679/
1 petitioner invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
However, since a Tribunal has already been constituted, liberty is given to the petitioner file an appeal as contemplated under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
___________________ P.KESHAVA
